liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Slewfoot** (3 reviews, 2 other sources): Slewfoot is called rare, played in a casual, laid-back first half of newer material; Rare Slewfoot features Garcia on pedal steel, showing country influence strongly on this date [1][2][5][7][11]
- **Dire Wolf** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Weir sings lead on Dire Wolf; Garcia plays pedal steel on Slewfoot, Green Green Grass of Home and Dire Wolf, leaving Weir to sing Dire Wolf [2][5][6][12][14]
- **Casey Jones** (3 reviews): Very early Casey Jones with a long instrumental lead-in and slower, groovy middle jams; still being worked out; Casey Jones here is one of the youngest versions posted [12][13][14]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (1 review): Bill loses the time badly during Dupree's Diamond Blues [11]
- **Big Boss Man** (1 review): Big Boss Man is described as smoking [10]
- **Green, Green Grass of Home** (1 review): The shift from The Eleven's driving power to the country twang of Green Green Grass of Home is jarring [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-06-27.166576.sbd.anon.gems.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 105 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.samaritano.20547.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 94 min; rated 4.1/5 by 20 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is very good overall, better than the reviewer's own cassette-to-CD copy; Reviewer finds the sound good but says their own cassette sounds fuller and equally crisp; Sounds quite good for its time, apart from some mixing flaws in part of Slewfoot [5][6][7][8][10]
- **gd1969-06-27.sbd.finney.10344.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 88 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [4]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.finney.78.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 93 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- Other artists listed: Hot Tuna, Joey Covington, and the Cleanliness & Godliness Skiffle Band [1]
- This early Casey Jones rocks differently than the faster, better-known later versions [12]
- Shows how softer later material grew out of the band's acid-laced country sound of the sixties [13]
- This early Casey Jones rocks differently than the faster, better-known later versions [14]
- Show displays both the emerging country side and the harder-driving side of the band in 1969 [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-06-27.166576.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: taped by Anon; transferred by Mastering by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: SBD master reel > DAT > AIFF [1]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.samaritano.20547.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: Soundboard (no DAE) [2]. Also: Reviewer previously had the show on a second-generation tape [7]
- **gd1969-06-27.sbd.finney.10344.shnf**: transferred by DFinnney and CPelz; source: SBD > Master Reel [4]. Also: Digitized from a cassette; original Slewfoot recording reportedly had levels set too high at first [4]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.finney.78.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Finney; source: Soundboard [3]
- Finney source is soundboard to master reel, with a glitch noted on D1T7 around 4:23 [20]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Veterans Auditorium - June 27, 1969](https://www.dead.net/show/june-27-1969) [22]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Veterans Auditorium, Santa Rosa Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/veterans-auditorium-santa-rosa-poster) [23]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1969-06-27 Fri Veterans Memorial Auditorium, Santa Rosa, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1389837363372/grateful-dead-1969-06-27-fri-veterans) [24]
